_about: Real open-source projects at pinned commits. must = fnmatch patterns over finding fingerprints the scan has to report (a real problem in that code); must_not = patterns it must never report (a false alarm, or a CVE the commit fixed); online_must = checked only with --online. Every expectation was checked by reading the code at the pinned commit; the reason is in 'why'. known_gaps = real problems the scan misses (or flags but shouldn't be counted): listed in RESULTS.md, not counted as failures.

repos.name: git-mcp-server
repos.kind: MCP server, commit before the CVE-2025-53107 fix

why.inject.shell|src/mcp-server/tools/gitSho: Builds `git -C "${targetPath}" show ${refSpec}` from tool input and runs it with promisify(exec). This is CVE-2025-53107.
why.inject.shell|src/mcp-server/tools/gitCom: Commit message and file paths pasted into a shell command (CVE-2025-53107).
why.inject.shell|src/mcp-server/tools/gitClo: Clone URL from tool input in a shell string (CVE-2025-53107).
why.ai.injection_risk: An MCP server: every tool argument is chosen by the model, so a prompt injection (the advisory's git-log example) reaches these commands.

repos.name: git-mcp-server-fixed
repos.kind: Same MCP server at the CVE-2025-53107 fix commit

why.inject.shell*: The fix replaced exec with execFile and argument arrays in every tool.
why.ai.injection_risk: Still an MCP server: tool input is model-chosen. This finding is about design, not the fixed bug.

repos.name: figma-context-mcp
repos.kind: MCP server, commit before the CVE-2025-53967 fix

Falls back to `curl ... "${url}"` run through promisify(exec). This is CVE-2025-53967.
why.ai.injection_risk: MCP server; the Figma URL and ids come from the model.
why.pkg.vulnerable|@modelcontextprotocol/sdk: pnpm-lock pins @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.10.2, which has published GHSA advisories.

repos.name: figma-context-mcp-fixed
repos.kind: Same MCP server at the CVE-2025-53967 fix commit

why.inject.shell*: The fix calls curl with execFile and an argument array.

why.inject.shell|src/handlers/comment-handle: `gh issue comment ${args.issue_number} ...` through execAsync, the exact lines the CVE-2025-53818 advisory links.
why.inject.shell|src/handlers/issue-handlers: Issue title, labels and numbers pasted into gh commands.
why.inject.shell|src/handlers/label-handlers: Label names pasted into gh commands.
why.ai.injection_risk: MCP server that also reads GitHub issues (untrusted text) into the model.
why.inject.shell|src/utils/exec.ts: Only defines the execAsync wrapper; the bug is where it's called.

repos.name: juice-shop
repos.kind: OWASP Juice Shop (deliberately insecure web shop)

why.inject.sql|routes/login.ts: sequelize.query with `${req.body.email}` in the SQL (login admin challenge).
why.inject.sql|routes/search.ts: Search criteria pasted into LIKE '%${criteria}%' (UNION injection challenge).
why.inject.eval|routes/userProfile.ts: eval(code) on part of the username (SSTI challenge).
why.secrets.hardcoded|lib/insecurity.ts: RSA private key for JWT signing in the source.
why.server.path|routes/fileServer.ts: res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/', file)) with file from params, guarded only by an extension check that the null-byte challenge bypasses.
why.server.redirect|routes/redirect.ts: res.redirect(toUrl) from query.to; the allowlist check uses includes() and is bypassable.
why.server.ssrf|routes/profileImageUrlUpload: fetch(url) with url from req.body.imageUrl (SSRF challenge).
why.xss.raw_html|frontend/src/app/track-resu: bypassSecurityTrustHtml with the order id (reflected XSS challenge).
why.inject.shell*: No shell commands built from input.

known_gaps.secrets.weak_hash: lib/insecurity.ts hashes passwords with MD5, but the word 'password' only appears where hash() is called in another file (routes/login.ts), so the scan doesn't connect them.
known_gaps.inject.eval|routes/captcha.ts: Also flagged (eval on a string), but the expression is built from random numbers on the server, so it isn't exploitable. Listed so nobody counts it as a catch.

why.inject.sql|transaction_db.py: get_user_transactions runs f"SELECT * FROM Transactions WHERE userId = '{str(userId)}'" with the userId the agent passes, the lab's intended prompt-to-SQL injection.
why.secrets.*: Keys come from .env, which isn't committed.

why.inject.shell|challenges/hard/challenge9/: _run_shell(cmd) runs subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) with tool input.
why.inject.eval|challenges/hard/challenge8/s: exec(code, ...) and eval(code) on tool input.
why.inject.eval|challenges/medium/challenge5: eval(expression, {'__builtins__': {}}) on tool input; the empty builtins don't make it safe.
why.aitools.tool_poisoning|challenges/easy/c: Tool docstring hides an <IMPORTANT> block telling the model to read and reveal internal://secret_config.
why.aitools.tool_poisoning|challenges/medium: Tool result appends hidden <IMPORTANT> instructions (rug pull).
why.aitools.tool_poisoning|challenges/hard/c: Tool description tells the model to call another tool.
why.aitools.tool_poisoning|challenges/supply: Tool text tells the model to read and send credentials.
why.secrets.hardcoded|challenges/easy/challe: A planted Stripe-style live key in the server config.
why.ai.injection_risk: MCP servers: tool input is model-chosen.
why.inject.sql*: Data is held in Python dicts, not SQL.

repos.name: saas-starter
repos.kind: Production template: Next.js, Stripe, Drizzle, own auth

why.xss.no_csp: next.config.ts sets no headers and there's no middleware CSP.
why.data.*: Data changes go through server actions that check the user with getUser(); no Supabase or Firebase.
why.server.*: No user-chosen URLs or file paths.

repos.name: chatbot
repos.kind: Production template: AI chat app (Vercel AI SDK, tools, Postgres)

why.xss.no_csp: No Content-Security-Policy in next.config.ts or middleware, and replies are rendered as markdown, so it's raised to medium.
why.inject.*: Drizzle queries; tools don't run code.
why.xss.raw_html*: dangerouslySetInnerHTML only for a constant theme script; innerHTML only with renderToString output.
why.data.*: Routes that write data (chat, document, history, vote) call auth() first; the ones without it are the NextAuth handlers and read-only lists.
why.ai.markdown_images|components/ai-element: Model replies render through Streamdown, whose shipped defaults (2.3.0) are allowedImagePrefixes: ["*"], so a reply can load an image from any host. No img-src CSP either.

repos.name: chatbot-ui
repos.kind: AI chat app: Supabase, file uploads, retrieval, custom tools

why.ai.injection_risk: Uploaded files are embedded and retrieved into the prompt, and the assistant can call user-defined tool APIs (app/api/chat/tools/route.ts).
why.data.rls_off*: Every table in supabase/migrations enables row level security.
why.ai.markdown_images|components/messages/m: react-markdown renders replies; the img override in message-markdown.tsx only adds a CSS class and passes any src through.

repos.name: nextjs-subscription-payments
repos.kind: Production template: Supabase auth and tables, Stripe

why.data.rls_off*: schema.sql enables RLS on every public table.
why.secrets.*: Env only; the service role key is only read server-side.

repos.name: taxonomy
repos.kind: Production template: Next.js, NextAuth, Prisma, Stripe

why.data.*: Routes that write data call getServerSession(); the Stripe webhook verifies the signature with constructEvent.

why.xss.raw_html|components/prose.tsx: Renders Shopify page HTML with dangerouslySetInnerHTML and no sanitizer. The store owner writes that HTML, so the risk is low, but anyone with Shopify admin access can put a script on the site; the finding is accurate.
